root_problem: The product-director standard chain needs a second small-demand pilot to prove the optimized handoffs stay clean across a different form-submission workflow.
business_goals: Deliver a small feedback form and thanks page experience through the full standard chain.
Collect direct evidence that product, design, implementation, review, QA, delivery, and user decision artifacts stay consumable when the feature is not authentication-centric.
acceptance_criteria: Root requests redirect visitors to the feedback form.
The feedback form exposes name and message fields.
Blank name or message submissions return a readable validation error.
Malformed negative Content-Length submissions return a readable validation error before reading the body.
Oversized form submissions return a readable too-large error.
Valid feedback submissions redirect to a thanks page with a generated id.
The thanks page renders submitted name and message using HTML escaping.
Unknown feedback ids return a readable not-found response.
Invalid submissions emit the default HTTP access log for auditability.
design_decisions: Use a Python standard-library HTTP example app to avoid introducing an unrelated product stack.
Store feedback submissions in memory behind a lock because the pilot only needs a local closed-loop workflow.
Escape submitted content before rendering the thanks page so the user-visible journey covers an XSS-sensitive boundary.
non_functional_requirements: Exercise the feature through a real local HTTP server, not a mocked request object.
Keep implementation and test files below the repository 400-line file limit.
Keep the pilot isolated under examples/feedback_thanks_app and tests/test_feedback_thanks_app.py.
Preserve BaseHTTPRequestHandler access logs so review and QA can observe negative paths.
Reject malformed negative Content-Length and oversized form bodies before accepting feedback.
scope_boundaries: In scope: feedback form, required-field validation, submission redirect, thanks page rendering, HTML escaping, missing-id handling, and canonical chain evidence.
Out of scope: persistence, authentication, browser CSS polish, production deployment, moderation workflow, and notification delivery.

delivery_plan.goal: ship and validate the feedback form plus thanks page pilot through a closed standard-chain run

director_confirmation.confirmation_basis: User delegated all standard-chain confirmations to Codex for the automated pilot.
